fact: The Bayesian Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters model predicted the observed patterns of generalization and learning rates better than a simple linear generalization model.
source_span: We found that the Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters Model predicts the pattern of generalisation and also the pattern of observed learning rates quite well and better than the simple linear generalisation prediction.
selection_reasoning: This fact states a key theoretical conclusion and model comparison relevant to the study's significance.

fact: The model predicts that learning multiple shape-mapping pairs simultaneously causes interference and slows overall learning rates.
source_span: When multiple pairs need to be learned simultaneously, these will interfere with each other due to the generalisation of local learning. The model therefore predicts a slow down of the overall learning rate with an increased number of shape-mapping pairs to be learned.
selection_reasoning: This fact explains an important mechanistic prediction of the model, relevant to understanding learning dynamics.

fact: The study’s findings are relevant to understanding how changes in visuomotor mappings, such as those caused by wearing optical glasses, are learned and generalized.

fact: The Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters model predicts generalisation behavior well by allowing learning for one shape to influence neighbouring shapes.

fact: Increasing the number of training pairs from 2 to 5 makes it harder to learn the linear relationship between shape and mapping.

fact: The Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters model predicts generalization patterns better than a linear model, especially in the 2-Pair condition.

selection_reasoning: This provides a mechanistic explanation for the observed decrease in learning with more training pairs, important for understanding the findings.

fact: Increased overlap between training conditions leads to longer learning times, which has practical implications such as longer adaptation periods for bifocal glasses compared to single focal length glasses.
source_span: This fact that learning times systematically increase with a decrease in spacing between the training conditions , even if they represent a simple relationship , can have major implications for daily life conditions . For instance , when acquiring bifocal glasses the learning time to get used to them can take quite a bit longer than for glasses having only a single focal length . Consistent with our model this increased familiarisation time would be due to the large discontinuity between the two focal areas leading to a large amount of learning overlap .
selection_reasoning: This connects the experimental findings to real-world relevance and illustrates the significance of the study.

fact: A control experiment showed substantial transfer of learning between the trained and untrained hand when two training pairs were used, confirming the role of explicit learning of contextual cues.

fact: Contextual cues are generally highly effective for learning simple amplitude gains or shifts in visual feedback, unlike in more complex force-field or visuomotor feedback rotation tasks where contextual cues are only effective under specific conditions.
source_span: Note that the ease of learning contextual cues in the current and previous experiments , seems in contrast to studies in which contextual cues were informative about force fields or visuomotor feedback rotations during reaching . In many of the latter studies , contextual cues were only effective under very specific circumstances ( see e . g . [32–39] ) whereas for the simpler amplitude gains or shifts of the visual feedback as used here , contextual cues are generally highly effective [8–18] .
selection_reasoning: This contextualizes the study's findings within the broader literature and clarifies the conditions under which contextual cue learning is effective.

fact: The dynamic and continuous error feedback in force-field or visuomotor rotation tasks may interfere with learning contextual cues by competing for attention and reducing the effectiveness of explicit strategies.
source_span: One of the major differences between the two types of studies is that the error information in force-field or visuomotor feedback rotations conditions is highly dynamic . That is , the sense of error increases during single movements , emphasising the role of online visual feedback to correct the movements in order to reach the target . Contextual cues would have to compete with the continuous feedback and dynamic error processing both in terms of attention—focussing on the feedback potentially makes it harder to apply an explicit strategy [40]—as well as the effectiveness for solving the task in general ( to reach the target , correcting for errors online is in principle sufficient ) .
selection_reasoning: This explains why contextual cue learning differs between simple and complex visuomotor tasks, a key insight for interpreting the results.

fact: The generalisation results were consistent across participants, suggesting a default strategy for interpolating and extrapolating to new shapes that does not rely solely on explicit rule application.
source_span: In light of the major role of explicit awareness for learning the contextual cues in the current study it is surprising that the generalisation results are so consistent across participants . This suggests that there is a default strategy for the interpolation and extrapolation to shapes that were not explicitly used in the training without participants particularly “choosing” a strategy for the new generalisation shapes .
selection_reasoning: This finding addresses the nature of generalisation in the learning process, an important aspect of the study's conclusions.

fact: The Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters model captures both the implicit learning component associated with each contextual cue and the interaction between learning processes for different target shapes.
source_span: In any case , the Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters seems to capture the learning process for contextual cues in visuomotor tasks and the “default generalisation strategy” quite well . That is , separate learning processes are maintained depending on the target shapes with some interaction between the learning processes . Note , that the Kalman-filter is often regarded as a model for automatic/implicit learning . The good correspondence between the Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters and our results thus suggests that , though explicit knowledge about the role of the contextual cues is necessary to separate the cue conditions , the learning process associated with each cue has an implicit learning component that is captured by the Kalman-filter .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the key modeling insight linking explicit awareness and implicit learning mechanisms, central to the study's interpretation.

fact: The PCM models identified novel HIV mutations that confer cross-resistance to multiple antiretroviral drugs, which were not previously published in the literature.
source_span: This led us to the next step of the study , the identification of novel mutations ( present in our dataset but not previously published ) which are found to confer cross resistance to antiretroviral treatments ... With these filters a number of novel resistance conferring mutations could successfully be identified which are listed in Table 2–4 .
selection_reasoning: Discovery of novel resistance mutations is a principal finding with translational relevance.

fact: The study also identified mutations that cause resistance to one specific drug but not to others in the same class, which is important for clinical treatment decisions.
source_span: We furthermore analyzed not only mutations that cause cross-resistance , but also those with a particular effect on a specific drug treatment alone . The goal here was to identify mutations that lead to large resistance for one drug but are still sensitive for another drug from the same class . Hence this knowledge can be of high importance in a clinical setting .
selection_reasoning: This finding has direct clinical relevance for optimizing HIV treatment.

fact: Proteochemometric modeling provides added value over sequence-only models by enabling deconvolution of individual mutation effects on drug resistance in HIV.
source_span: The purpose of this validation was therefore twofold , to assess the performance of PCM when compared to sequence only models , and secondly to assess if the PCM models can deconvolute the effect of individual mutations to make accurate predictions for mixture sequences .
selection_reasoning: This explains the motivation and significance of using PCM models, a key background and methodological claim.

fact: Mutations can cause resistance to one drug while increasing sensitivity to another drug within the same class of protease inhibitors.
source_span: In those figures we can observe several mutations that lead to resistance for a single drug ( Log FC on average >0 . 5 ) and at the same time lead to higher sensitivity for another drug ( Log FC on average <0 . 0 ) . For instance , the G48W mutant is sensitive to Darunavir and Tipranavir , while showing some degree of resistance to all other PIs . Furthermore , R87K is resistant to Atazanavir , Darunavir , and Tipranavir , but sensitive to all other drugs in the dataset . Finally , N88G seems to only be sensitive to Darunavir , while conferring resistance to all other PIs in the dataset .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key finding about differential drug resistance mutations, which is important for personalized treatment decisions.

fact: Linking viral genotype to clinical phenotype can help prescribe the optimal drug for an individual patient.
source_span: Information of this type is of high relevance to prescribe the optimal drug for an individual patient , by being able to link the viral genotype to the clinical phenotype in a real-world situation .
selection_reasoning: This fact states the clinical significance and motivation for studying mutation-specific drug resistance.

fact: The study developed models that predict which HIV drugs will be least affected by resistance based on a patient's viral genotype.
source_span: Given a sequence of PR and RT ( and hence , a viral genotype of a patient to be treated ) , our models are able to predict which drugs will be least influenced by resistance , as measured via the lowest Log FC .
selection_reasoning: This describes the main methodological approach and its purpose, central to the study's contribution.

fact: The models were validated on unseen clinical data from the Stanford University HIV Drug Resistance Database to assess prospective prediction accuracy.
source_span: To accurately estimate our model performance in prospective predictions , in the final step of this study we performed a validation on unseen data . Apart from only focusing on unseen data , in order to establish agreement of our modeling procedure with other approaches , we also employed data from an entirely different source – namely , for sequences obtained from the Stanford University HIV Drug Resistance Database ( Stanford Set ) .
selection_reasoning: Validation on independent data is a key step demonstrating the model's real-world applicability.

fact: The protease inhibitor (PI) model showed the best predictive performance with an RMSE of 0.43 log units and R² of 0.76 on the Stanford dataset.
source_span: The PI model again performs the best ( with an RMSE of 0 . 43 log units and an R02 of 0 . 76 )
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the principal finding about model accuracy, important for evaluating clinical utility.

fact: The non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) model had the largest prediction error due to several outliers in the dataset.
source_span: while the NNRTIs are predicted with the largest error ( with an RMSE of 0 . 62 log units and an R02 of 0 . 66 ) , which is the result of a number of outliers
selection_reasoning: This identifies limitations in model performance, relevant for interpreting results.

fact: Differences in reported drug resistance values across literature sources can adversely affect model performance.
source_span: Overall , when the results are grouped per literature reference number ( which is included in the dataset ) the average quality decreases and the standard deviation increases , indicating that differences between reported Log FC changes in literature exist and this could adversely affect model performance .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key challenge in modeling and data reliability, important for understanding study context.

fact: The model correctly classified drug resistance response in 84% of cases overall, with accuracy varying by drug class (PI 85%, NNRTI 89%, NRTI 79%).
source_span: Our model classifies the response correctly in 84% of the cases ( Table 5 ) . The average performance when grouped per individual drug class was very good ( PI 85% , NNRTI 89% and NRTI 79% ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the key performance metric demonstrating the model's clinical relevance.

fact: The model tends to overpredict resistance rather than underpredict it, which is especially relevant in a clinical setting.
source_span: Also noteworthy is that the model bias is towards over prediction rather than under prediction , something that is not always mentioned in literature but is especially relevant in a clinical setting .
selection_reasoning: This fact addresses an important aspect of model behavior affecting clinical decision-making.

fact: This work reports the construction of robust proteochemometric (PCM) models based on 300,000 bioactivity data points measured against different HIV genotypes.
source_span: In this work we report the construction of robust PCM models, based on 300,000 bioactivity data points measured against different HIV genotypes.
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the main methodological advance and dataset scale, which is central to the study.

fact: The PCM models combined resistance profiles of three HIV drug classes (PI, NNRTI, and NRTI) into three single models covering tens of thousands of different protein mutants.
source_span: Given the nature of the PCM modeling procedure employed in this work, we were able to combine all resistance profiles of the three above drug classes in three single models, hence focusing on very large target space (tens of thousands of different proteins) in this work.
selection_reasoning: This highlights the scope and novelty of the modeling approach relevant to the study's main question.

fact: The PCM models showed performance comparable to assay reliability and better than sequence-only models in both internal validation and validation on unseen data.
source_span: Both in internal validation and validation on unseen data our model showed performance comparable to assay reliability and better than sequence only models;
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes key model performance results important for the study's conclusions.

fact: Model interpretation identified novel resistance-conferring mutations that cause resistance to all drugs in a class, such as T216M in reverse transcriptase.
source_span: Moreover, model interpretation has been performed to identify novel resistance-conferring mutations that lead to resistance to all drugs in a class, such as T216M in the case of RT.
selection_reasoning: This finding is a principal biological insight derived from the models, relevant for understanding resistance mechanisms.

fact: The models can also identify mutations that cause specific sensitivity or resistance to a single drug within a class, such as G48W causing sensitivity and G68R causing resistance in protease.
source_span: In addition, we can use these models to find mutations that lead specific sensitivity (G48W in PR) or resistance (G68R in PR) to a single drug within a class.
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the models' ability to predict drug-specific mutation effects, important for personalized treatment.

fact: The PCM models can support personalized drug regimen predictions by reliably predicting clinical resistance.
source_span: Another application of our models is the support of personalized drug regimen predictions. We have shown that our models are able to predict clinical resistance with a high degree of reliability.
selection_reasoning: This fact states the clinical relevance and translational potential of the models.

fact: The models achieved a 95% correct classification percentage (CCP) when predicting clinical response for Antivirogram data, which the models were trained on.
source_span: This reliability is formed by a 95% CCP when predicting clinical response for Antivirogram data, which is the assay models were trained on,
selection_reasoning: This quantifies the high accuracy of the models on training assay data, supporting their validity.

fact: The models achieved up to 81% CCP when predicting clinical response for unknown mutants and 84% CCP for clinical isolates from diverse sources, demonstrating robustness and predictive power.
source_span: Furthermore, the CCP and is as high as 81% when predicting clinical response for unknown mutants. ... Finally, the CCP is 84% when predicting clinical response for clinical isolates obtained from very diverse sources (including historical literature data and data from different assays), indicating that the model is robust and predictive.
selection_reasoning: This fact emphasizes the model's novelty and robustness in predicting resistance for previously unseen variants.

fact: The improved performance of PCM models is attributed to training on a large co-linked dataset and encoding full sequences using physicochemical properties rather than just mutation presence or absence.
source_span: We attribute the better performance of PCM to two reasons. Firstly our models are trained on a very large co-linked dataset. ... The second reason is related to the first, as the encoding of the full sequences using physicochemical properties rather than presence or absence of mutations allows for a better similarity measure between two sequences.
selection_reasoning: This explains the methodological innovation underlying the improved model performance.

fact: The main dataset was obtained from Virco and consisted of protease and reverse transcriptase mutants with fold change data in pIC50 from the AVG assay collected up to January 2011.
source_span: The main dataset was obtained from Virco (Beerse, Belgium) and consisted of mutants (both PR and RT sequences) and fold change (Log FC) in pIC50 (log units) data in the AVG assay collected by Virco up to January 2011.
selection_reasoning: This fact provides important background on the data source and type used for model training.

fact: Sequences were encoded using Z-scales, which characterize physicochemical properties of amino acid side chains such as lipophilicity, size, and polarity.
source_span: Sequences were subsequently encoded using the first three Z-scales. The Z-scales are a previously published set of descriptors that characterize the physicochemical properties of the amino acids side chains. The resulting scales correlate to lipophilicity, size and polarity for each amino acid.
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key methodological step relevant to how the models represent sequence data.

fact: Drug structures were normalized, ionized at pH 7.4, and converted to circular fingerprints (ECFP) to create numeric descriptors for each drug.
source_span: Structures of the drugs were normalized and ionized at pH 7.4, they were assigned 2D coordinates and subsequently converted to Scitegic circular fingerprints of type ECFP_8, ECFP_10 and ECFP_12 (depending on drug class, as described below).
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the approach used to represent drug chemical structures, important for the PCM modeling.

fact: Proteochemometric (PCM) models were constructed using support vector machines to predict drug resistance based on HIV mutant sequences and drug features.
source_span: Models were constructed in the academic version of Pipeline Pilot 6 . 1 . 5 using the R-statistics package . Support vector machines ( SVM ) with a radial basis function kernel as coded in the e1071 package were used for model creation .
selection_reasoning: This describes the key modeling approach used to predict drug resistance, central to the study's main question and methods.

fact: The applicability domain of the models was defined based on the density of nearest neighbor sequences in the training set, using a 97% sequence similarity threshold.
source_span: Rather we choose to determine the applicability domain based on the density of the nearest neighbors in the training set . This density was expressed as the fraction of the total number of sequences meeting a certain similarity criterion . ... Optimal performance was reached at 97% , similarity defined as 1 minus the euclidean distance .
selection_reasoning: Defining the applicability domain is important for understanding the model's reliability and generalizability, a key methodological and interpretative point.

fact: The PCM models showed robust performance with good validation parameters, with the protease inhibitor (PI) model performing best and the non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) model performing worst.
source_span: The results show that PCM is not only able to create models on this data , but also that these models are robust with good validation parameters . The PI model shows the best performance , RMSE = 0 . 42 log units when trained on 5% of the full set and <0 . 30 log units when trained on 70% of the dataset . The NNRTI model the worst performance , RMSE = 0 . 70 log units when trained on 5% of the full set and <0 . 50 log units when trained on 70% of the dataset .
selection_reasoning: Reporting model performance and differences between drug classes is a principal finding relevant to the study's conclusions.

fact: Models trained on scrambled data showed no predictive power, confirming that the original models capture meaningful relationships between mutations and drug resistance.
source_span: Models that were trained on this scrambled set and validated on 30% the data that was kept unscrambled produced very high RMSE values ... Furthermore , the values for the R02 were very low ... Finally the cross validation parameters for the models trained on these scrambled sets demonstrated a lack of correlation ... The corresponding correlation coefficient was 0 . 00 for all three models .
selection_reasoning: This negative control validates the model's predictive ability, a key methodological and interpretative claim.

fact: The effect of individual amino acid residues on drug resistance was assessed by in silico mutation back to wild type and comparing model predictions, providing interpretability of the models.
source_span: To determine the effect of individual residues , for each sequence each residue was mutated back to wild type in silico by replacing the descriptors of the mutant amino acid with the descriptors of the corresponding wild type residue ... The difference was interpreted as the change in pIC50 induced by that particular residue , hence providing model interpretability .
selection_reasoning: This approach to interpret model predictions is a key methodological innovation and supports biological insight.

fact: Known resistance mutations were compared to model interpretations to validate the model's ability to identify mutations that increase drug resistance.
source_span: Known resistant mutations were retrieved from earlier publications by Johnson et al. and compared to our model interpretation ... they are a good frame of reference for our model interpretation .
selection_reasoning: Comparing model findings to known resistance mutations supports the model's biological relevance and significance.

fact: Novel mutations that increase drug resistance were identified by filtering mutations with a negative effect on most drugs in a class, occurring multiple times, and having an average fold change above a threshold, excluding previously known mutations.
source_span: Mutations were filtered using the following parameters: have a negative effect on the majority of drugs in a single class; occurrence in the dataset more than once; average Log FC for all compounds >0 . 4; standard deviation over this average <0 . 4 . ... using literature we discarded any previously known mutations and kept those mutations that were novel .
selection_reasoning: Identifying novel resistance mutations is a principal finding with translational significance.

fact: The study identified novel mutations that lead to an average increase in drug resistance fold change across multiple drugs within a class.
source_span: This provided us with a number of mutations that lead to an increase in fold change on average , again using literature we discarded any previously known mutations and kept those mutations that were novel .
selection_reasoning: Identifying novel resistance mutations is a core finding relevant to understanding drug resistance mechanisms.

fact: The dataset used to compare proteochemometric (PCM) models with sequence-only models was obtained from Van der Borght et al. and included sequences with the largest prediction errors per drug class.
source_span: The dataset we used to compare the performance of PCM models with sequence only models was obtained from Van der Borght et al . [39] From the paper the 150 sequences with the largest prediction error were selected per drug class .
selection_reasoning: Describing the dataset and comparison approach is important for understanding the study's evaluation of predictive models.

fact: The study excluded mixtures with more than four possible variants at a single position, resulting in 146 NNRTI sequences, 146 NRTI sequences, and 149 PI sequences for analysis.
source_span: Mixtures with more than four possible variants at a single position were discarded leading to a total of 146 NNRTI sequences , 146 NRTI sequences , and 149 PI sequences .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the dataset composition used for model evaluation, relevant to the study methods.

fact: The Phenosense assay is more quantitative than the AVG assay, but the correlation between their resistance measurements is not very strong.
source_span: Prediction of the Stanford University set is of is of particular interest since the correlation between Phenosense and AVG has previously been shown not to be very strong . [63] , [64] Yet it should also be noted that the Phenosense assay is in fact more quantitative .
selection_reasoning: Understanding assay differences is important for interpreting resistance prediction accuracy and clinical relevance.

fact: There are discrepancies in resistance predictions between Phenosense and AVG assays for specific mutations such as M41L, M184V, and T215Y.
source_span: In particular for mutations M41L , M184V , and T215Y there are differences in Phenosense predictions compared with AVG . [65]
selection_reasoning: Highlighting mutation-specific assay discrepancies is relevant to the study's evaluation of prediction models.

fact: The resistance profiles of drugs d4T and TDF show a Pearson's correlation coefficient below 0.8 between Phenosense and VircoTYPE assays.
source_span: For instance the resistance profile of d4T and TDF , have been shown to have a Pearson's correlation coefficient <0 . 8 between the two assays . [51]
selection_reasoning: This fact illustrates assay variability affecting resistance measurement, important for clinical interpretation.

fact: Sequences present in the Virco training set were removed from the Stanford reference set to avoid artificially boosting prediction results.
source_span: The reference set was downloaded from the Stanford website ( version 5 . 0 , July 30 , 2010 ) , from this set the sequences by Virco were removed ( as they are presumed to be in the training set , and this would artificially boost the results ) .
selection_reasoning: Ensuring unbiased validation is critical for credible model performance assessment.

fact: The study predicted Log fold change values for individual drug-mutant pairs and calculated validation parameters grouped by sequence, isolate, reference ID, drug, and drug class.
source_span: After we predicted the Log FC values for individual drug – mutant pairs using our models , the validation parameters were calculated grouped by: Sequence ID ( average and standard deviation ) , per Isolate ( average and standard deviation ) , per Reference ID ( average and standard deviation ) , per drug ( average and standard deviation ) , per class ( total ) , and per individual drug ( total ) ( Table 5 ) .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the key analytical approach used to evaluate model predictions.

fact: Resistance was classified using clinical cut-offs from the Stanford website and AVG values from Virco, allowing calculation of clinical classification performance including over- and underprediction rates.
source_span: Resistance was also classified using clinical cut-offs ( CCOs ) , here we used the values provided on the Stanford website and the values from AVG were obtained from Virco ( supporting Table S10 and supporting Table S11 ) . Subsequently CCP was calculated as a fraction of the total , in addition the fraction of overpredicted clinical response ( resistance is predicted higher than measured experimentally ) and underpredicted clinical response ( resistance is predicted lower than measured experimentally ) is included .
selection_reasoning: This fact relates to the clinical relevance and accuracy of resistance predictions, a key study outcome.

fact: Staphylococcus aureus expresses cell wall-anchored proteins that mediate adhesion, invasion, and immune evasion, contributing to its virulence.
source_span: Staphylococcus aureus expresses a number of cell wall-anchored proteins that mediate adhesion and invasion of host cells and tissues and promote immune evasion , consequently contributing to the virulence of this organism .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the biological basis for S. aureus virulence and sets the stage for studying specific surface proteins.

fact: Clumping factor B (ClfB) facilitates Staphylococcus aureus nasal colonization through high affinity interactions with the cornified envelope in the anterior nares.
source_span: The cell wall-anchored protein clumping factor B ( ClfB ) has previously been shown to facilitate S . aureus nasal colonization through high affinity interactions with the cornified envelope in the anterior nares .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides important background on the known role of ClfB relevant to colonization, motivating investigation of its role in skin infection.

fact: The role of ClfB during skin and soft tissue infection (SSTI) had not been previously investigated.
source_span: However , the role of ClfB during skin and soft tissue infection ( SSTI ) has never been investigated .
selection_reasoning: This identifies the knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

fact: This study reveals a novel role for ClfB during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections.
source_span: This study reveals a novel role for ClfB during SSTIs .
selection_reasoning: This statement highlights the main research finding.

fact: ClfB is crucial in determining abscess structure and bacterial burden early in skin infection through a specific interaction with the ligand loricrin expressed in abscess tissue.
source_span: ClfB is crucial in determining the abscess structure and bacterial burden early in infection and this is dependent upon a specific interaction with the ligand loricrin which is expressed within the abscess tissue .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key mechanism and principal finding of the study.

fact: Targeting ClfB with a model vaccine that induces protective humoral and cellular responses leads to protection during Staphylococcus aureus skin infection.
source_span: Targeting ClfB using a model vaccine that induced both protective humoral and cellular responses , leads to protection during S . aureus skin infection .
selection_reasoning: This fact shows the translational significance and therapeutic potential of ClfB as a vaccine target.

fact: ClfB is identified as an important antigen for future vaccines against skin and soft tissue infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus.
source_span: This study therefore identifies ClfB as an important antigen for future SSTI vaccines .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the study's implication for vaccine development.

fact: Staphylococcus aureus is the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections in humans, resulting in millions of outpatient visits and hundreds of thousands of hospital admissions annually in the United States.
source_span: Staphylococcus aureus is the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections ( SSTIs ) in humans [1 , 2] with S . aureus SSTIs resulting in over 11 million outpatient visits and almost 500 , 000 hospital admissions in the United States annually [3] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact establishes the public health importance of S. aureus SSTIs.

fact: Skin abscesses caused by Staphylococcus aureus limit antibiotic penetration and efficacy.
source_span: S . aureus SSTIs routinely manifest as cutaneous abscesses which limit the penetration and efficacy of antibiotics [4] .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains why SSTIs are difficult to treat and why alternative therapies like vaccines are needed.

fact: Community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA) skin infections are increasing in healthy individuals and are difficult to treat due to antibiotic resistance.
source_span: Community-acquired methicillin resistant S . aureus ( CA-MRSA ) skin infections are increasing in frequency in healthy individuals [5] and the treatment of these infections has become increasingly difficult due to the emergence of antibiotic resistance .
selection_reasoning: This fact motivates the need for vaccine development as an alternative to antibiotics.

fact: An effective universal vaccine against Staphylococcus aureus is unlikely, so vaccines targeting specific clinical manifestations such as skin and soft tissue infections may be necessary.
source_span: Given the wide spectrum of pathologies caused by this bacterium it is unlikely that a universal anti-S . aureus vaccine will ever be realised [6] , and instead , a vaccine targeting specific clinical manifestations may need to be pursued .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides rationale for focusing vaccine development on SSTIs.

fact: Cell wall-anchored proteins are important for Staphylococcus aureus virulence during skin and soft tissue infections and may be particularly important during abscess formation.
source_span: These studies indicate that CWA proteins are important during SSTIs and suggest that CWA proteins may be particularly important during the process of abscess formation .
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the study focus on ClfB, a cell wall-anchored protein.

fact: Clumping factor A (ClfA) plays a role in Staphylococcus aureus skin infection, but vaccines targeting ClfA provide only modest protection, suggesting other surface proteins like ClfB may be important.
source_span: Clumping factor A has previously been shown to play a role in the pathogenesis of S . aureus SSTI , as mice inoculated with a ClfA-deficient mutant of S . aureus strain Newman demonstrated a lower bacterial burden in the skin compared to the wild type strain at Day 2 post-inoculation [11] . However , vaccination strategies targeting ClfA only provided modest protection in this model [12] suggesting that other surface proteins may also play an important role in the development of S . aureus SSTI .
selection_reasoning: This fact justifies investigating ClfB as an alternative vaccine target.

fact: ClfB binds to plasma fibrinogen, cytokeratin 10, and loricrin, with loricrin being a critical ligand for ClfB in vivo in mice.
source_span: ClfB binds to plasma fibrinogen [19] , cytokeratin 10 [20] , which is the dominant component of the interior of squamous cells , and to loricrin , which is the most abundant protein of the cornified envelope of squamous cells [21] . Rates of S . aureus nasal colonization were significantly reduced in loricrin-knockout mice compared to wild-type mice , demonstrating that loricrin is a critical ligand for ClfB in vivo , at least in mice [13] .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the molecular interaction underlying ClfB function relevant to infection.

fact: Mice infected with a ClfB-deficient Staphylococcus aureus strain formed significantly smaller abscess lesions and had reduced bacterial burden compared to mice infected with the wild-type strain.
source_span: Mice infected with LAC::lux ΔclfB formed significantly smaller abscess lesions on day 3–6 compared to mice infected with LAC::lux ( Fig 1A and 1B ) . The bioluminescence signal was also reduced in LAC::lux ΔclfB infected animals compared to LAC::lux infected mice ( Fig 1C and 1D ) . The reduction in bioluminescence signal was validated by quantifying the bacterial burden in the skin on day 3 ( Fig 1E ) and day 6 ( Fig 1F ) .
selection_reasoning: This experimental result directly supports the key finding that ClfB contributes to SSTI severity.

fact: ClfB affects both the rate of abscess formation and the overall size of the abscess formed during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections.
source_span: Taken together, these results demonstrate that ClfB affects both the rate of abscess formation and the overall size of the abscess formed, which ultimately leads to greater bacterial burden in the skin.
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding linking ClfB to abscess development and bacterial burden, central to the study's main question and significance.

fact: ClfB has an important function during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections, likely exerting its effect early in the infection process.
source_span: Crucially, these results have demonstrated for the first time that ClfB has an important function during S. aureus SSTIs, likely exerting its effect early in the infection process.
selection_reasoning: This highlights the novel discovery and timing of ClfB's role, important background and main conclusion.

fact: During nasal colonization, Staphylococcus aureus binding to the squamous epithelium is facilitated by the interaction between ClfB and the squamous cell envelope protein loricrin.
source_span: During nasal colonization, S. aureus binding to the squamous epithelium of the anterior nares is facilitated via the interaction between ClfB and the squamous cell envelope protein loricrin.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the known ClfB-loricrin interaction, providing biological context for the study.

fact: Loricrin is present in the epidermal layer and in the abscess wall structure during Staphylococcus aureus subcutaneous abscess formation.
source_span: At 48 h post-infection loricrin is clearly visible in the epidermal layer of the skin, which is to be expected as it is a major component of the cornified envelope. Interestingly, it is also detected in the abscess wall structure following challenge with both LAC::lux and LAC::lux ΔclfB.
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the relevance of loricrin in the infected tissue, linking to the mechanism of ClfB binding during infection.

fact: Loricrin-deficient mice form significantly smaller abscesses and have reduced bacterial burden during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections compared to wild-type mice.
source_span: Lor-/- mice formed significantly smaller abscesses compared to WT mice and had reduced bioluminescence, indicating the presence of loricrin is important for abscess formation and bacterial burden during S. aureus SSTIs.
selection_reasoning: This finding demonstrates the functional importance of loricrin in abscess formation and bacterial growth, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: Abscess formation is impaired in loricrin-deficient mice at 12 hours post infection, with less well-structured and smaller abscesses formed.
source_span: Importantly, it can be seen that abscess formation is impaired in Lor-/- mice at 12 hours post infection with overall less well-structured and smaller abscesses being formed.
selection_reasoning: This supports the early role of loricrin in abscess development, reinforcing the timing and mechanism of infection.

fact: In wild-type mice, infection with Staphylococcus aureus lacking ClfB results in smaller abscess lesions and reduced bacterial burden compared to infection with wild-type bacteria.
source_span: WT mice that received LAC::lux ΔclfB formed smaller abscess lesions and had significantly reduced bioluminescence compared to WT mice that received LAC::lux which was confirmed by quantifying bacterial burden in the skin.
selection_reasoning: This directly links ClfB expression to virulence and abscess severity, a core experimental finding.

fact: In loricrin-deficient mice, there is no significant difference in abscess size or bacterial burden between infection with Staphylococcus aureus expressing ClfB and bacteria lacking ClfB.
source_span: There was no significant difference in abscess lesion area, bioluminescence or skin CFUs between Lor-/- mice that received LAC::lux or LAC::lux ΔclfB.
selection_reasoning: This shows that loricrin is required for ClfB-dependent virulence, clarifying the mechanism of interaction.

fact: Recombinant loricrin loop L2v can block the interaction between ClfB and its native ligands, reducing abscess lesion size and bacterial burden during Staphylococcus aureus skin infection.
source_span: Mice that received LAC::lux pre-incubated with L2v had reduced abscess lesion area compared to the LAC::lux+GST group. In addition, bioluminescence signal was reduced throughout the infection period in LAC::lux+L2v infected mice compared to mice that received LAC::lux+GST and this reduction in bioluminescence was confirmed with a significant decrease in the bacterial burden in the skin on day 3 and 6 post-infection.
selection_reasoning: This demonstrates a potential therapeutic approach targeting the ClfB-loricrin interaction.

fact: Vaccination with ClfB combined with the TLR9 agonist CpG induces antigen-specific cellular and humoral immune responses in mice.
source_span: Immunization with ClfB in combination with CpG drove a significant increase in ClfB-specific IFNγ, IL-17 and IL-22 producing CD4+ T cells by inguinal lymph node cells compared to CpG-immunized mice. ClfB-specific CD8+ T cells producing IFNγ, IL-17 and IL-22 were also increased. Vaccination with ClfB also induced significantly elevated ClfB-specific serum IgG titres in mice compared to the control group.
selection_reasoning: This is a key translational finding showing the vaccine candidate elicits relevant immune responses.

fact: Antibodies induced by ClfB vaccination can inhibit the binding of ClfB-expressing bacteria to loricrin.
source_span: We confirmed that these antibodies were functional by investigating their ability to inhibit L. lactis expressing ClfB to bind to immobilised loricrin.
selection_reasoning: This supports the functional relevance of the vaccine-induced antibodies, linking immune response to mechanism.

fact: ClfB is a surface protein of Staphylococcus aureus that was previously known to facilitate nasal colonization by binding to host ligands loricrin and cytokeratin 10.
source_span: Previous to this study , the main function attributed to ClfB was in facilitating S . aureus nasal colonization due to its ability to bind host ligands loricrin and cytokeratin 10 in the anterior nares [13–15].
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the known role of ClfB and sets the stage for investigating its role in skin infections.

fact: This study identifies ClfB as a virulence factor that contributes to the pathogenesis of Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections (SSTIs).
source_span: This study identifies , for the first time , an important role for ClfB in the pathogenesis of SSTIs and provides proof-of-concept that ClfB represents a good candidate antigen for inclusion in next-generation vaccines targeting S . aureus SSTI.
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding that expands the known role of ClfB and motivates vaccine development.

fact: Using a ClfB mutant strain of the clinically relevant CA-MRSA USA300 strain, the study demonstrates that ClfB is important for early abscess formation during skin infection.
source_span: Using a clfB mutant in the clinically relevant CA-MRSA USA300 strain , LAC::lux , we demonstrate that ClfB is a virulence determinant during S . aureus skin infection . Crucially , ClfB appears to exert its effect early during the infection process during initial formation of the abscess.
selection_reasoning: This mechanistic insight supports the role of ClfB in SSTI pathogenesis and is central to the study's claims.

fact: Loricrin, a host ligand for ClfB, is present not only in the outer skin layers but also within the abscess wall during infection, suggesting that loricrin expression is altered during wound healing and facilitates bacterial binding.
source_span: Immunohistochemistry analysis revealed that loricrin , an important ligand for ClfB , was present in the outermost layer of the skin , the corneal layer , as expected; however , loricrin also appeared to be present within the wall of the skin abscess structure of LAC::lux infected mice . selection_reasoning: This explains a key molecular mechanism underlying cadmium sensitivity and cell cycle arrest recovery, central to the study's findings.

fact: The cell cycle checkpoint arrest induced by deubiquitylated Met4 to cope with cadmium stress is maintained longer in MET30M178E/I179E mutants, causing apparent cadmium sensitivity.
source_span: The cell cycle checkpoint arrest, initially induced by deubiquitylated Met4 to cope with cadmium stress, may therefore be erroneously maintained in MET30M178E/I179E mutants resulting in apparent cadmium sensitivity.
selection_reasoning: This links the mutant phenotype to a failure in cell cycle recovery, a principal finding relevant to the study's biological and stress response context.

fact: Deletion of MET32 suppresses the growth defect of MET30M178E/I179E mutants under cadmium stress by allowing timely inactivation of Met4.
source_span: Deletion of MET32 suppressed the growth defect of cells expressing Met30M178E/I179E under cadmium stress, indicating that excess dissociated Met30M178E/I179E interferes with timely inactivation of Met4.
selection_reasoning: This genetic evidence supports the proposed mechanism and is a key experimental result validating the hypothesis.

fact: Met4 target genes MET3 and GSH1 are derepressed in Met30M178E/I179E mutants, confirming untimely Met4 activation.
source_span: Two tested Met4 target genes, MET3 and GSH1, were derepressed in Met30M178E/I179E mutants confirming untimely Met4 activation.
selection_reasoning: This molecular evidence confirms the functional consequence of the mutant Met30 on Met4 activity, a core finding.

fact: The 'Skp1-free' F-box protein degradation pathway prevents substrate shielding effects by degrading excess unbound F-box proteins.
source_span: Together, these results indicate that the ‘Skp1-free’ F-box protein degradation pathway plays an important role in cellular function to prevent substrate shielding effects by excess unbound F-box proteins.
selection_reasoning: This identifies the novel degradation pathway as a key regulatory mechanism, central to the study's significance.

fact: Met30M178E/I179E mutants show increased chromosome loss, suggesting additional cellular defects linked to stabilized Met30.
source_span: In addition to enhanced cadmium sensitivity, Met30M178E/I179E mutants displayed increased chromosome loss.
selection_reasoning: This finding extends the biological impact of the mutant beyond cadmium sensitivity, highlighting broader cellular consequences.

fact: The study describes a novel pathway that degrades F-box proteins dissociated from Skp1, maintaining F-box protein homeostasis.
source_span: We describe a novel pathway for regulation of F-box protein abundance in addition to autoubiquitylation that specifically targets F-box proteins that are dissociated from Skp1.
selection_reasoning: This is the main discovery of the study, providing background and motivation for the research.

fact: F-box proteins bound to Skp1 form functional SCF ligases, while unbound F-box proteins are targeted for degradation by the Cdc53/Rbx1 ligase.
source_span: F-box proteins that associate with Skp1 form functional ligases while those that do not, are recognized by the ‘Skp1-free’ F-box protein degradation pathway and degraded by the Cdc53/Rbx1 ligase.
selection_reasoning: This mechanistic insight explains how cells regulate SCF complex composition and prevent competition among F-box proteins.

fact: Degradation of unbound F-box proteins may serve as a quality control mechanism to remove damaged F-box proteins that could otherwise shield substrates from degradation.
source_span: Degradation of F-box proteins that are not bound to Skp1 may also provide an important quality control mechanism to remove damaged F-box proteins.
selection_reasoning: This implication highlights the biological importance and significance of the newly described pathway.

fact: The 'Skp1-free' F-box protein degradation pathway is particularly important for Met30 because Met4 ubiquitylation by SCFMet30 does not induce Met4 degradation, allowing Met4 to remain bound to Met30 and prevent autoubiquitylation-based degradation.
source_span: The ‘Skp1-free’ F-box protein degradation pathway is of particular importance for Met30. First, because Met4 ubiquitylation does not induce its degradation under normal growth conditions, Met4 remains associated with Met30 and therefore prevents the canonical F-box-protein degradation pathway through autoubiquitylation.
selection_reasoning: This explains why Met30 relies on the novel degradation pathway, a key mechanistic detail.

fact: Heavy metal stress induces dissociation of Met30 from Skp1, increasing 'Skp1-free' Met30 that interferes with recovery from cadmium stress when the degradation pathway is blocked.
source_span: Heavy metal stress induces active dissociation of Met30 from Skp1 resulting in a burst of ‘Skp1-free’ Met30, which interferes with recovery from cadmium stress when the ‘Skp1-free’ degradation pathway is blocked.
selection_reasoning: This links environmental stress to the regulation of Met30 and the importance of the degradation pathway in stress recovery.

fact: Other essential yeast F-box proteins, Cdc4 and Ctf13, are also degraded in the absence of Skp1, suggesting the pathway is a common mechanism to restrict F-box protein abundance outside the SCF complex.
source_span: Apart from Met30, the two other essential yeast F-box proteins—Cdc4 and Ctf13 are also degraded in the absence of Skp1, suggesting that this pathway is a common mechanism to restrict F-box protein abundance outside the SCF complex.
selection_reasoning: This generalizes the pathway beyond Met30, increasing its biological significance.

fact: Not all F-box proteins are subject to the 'Skp1-free' degradation pathway; for example, Grr1 is stabilized when its F-box region is deleted or Skp1 is inactivated.
source_span: Not all F-box proteins are subject to this degradation mechanism, because consistent with other reports we found that deletion of the F-box region in Grr1 or inactivation of Skp1 stabilized Grr1.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the specificity and limits of the pathway, important for understanding its scope.

fact: The 'Skp1-free' F-box protein degradation pathway requires a hydrophobic region adjacent to the F-box domain for Cdc53/Rbx1 ligase binding.
source_span: The F-box protein degradation pathway we describe here is probably functional for only those F-box proteins which harbor the hydrophobic region adjacent to the F-box domain, which is paramount for Cdc53/Rbx1 ligase binding.
selection_reasoning: This identifies a structural requirement for pathway targeting, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: Cdc53 (cullin-1) has a function independent of its adaptor Skp1, as it can mediate Met30 degradation without Skp1 both in vivo and in vitro.
source_span: Not only was Met30 degradation active in the absence of Skp1 in vivo, but in addition a Cdc53 mutant incapable of binding to Skp1 could fully complement the Met30 degradation defect of cdc53 mutants.
selection_reasoning: This reveals a novel functional role for Cdc53, expanding understanding of ubiquitin ligase regulation.

fact: Cdc53/Rbx1 can directly bind Met30 in the absence of Skp1 in vitro, and this binding depends on the degron region adjacent to the F-box motif.
source_span: Cdc53/Rbx1 can directly bind Met30 in the absence of Skp1 in vitro and binding depends on the degron region adjacent to the F-box motif.
selection_reasoning: This provides biochemical evidence supporting the novel degradation mechanism.

fact: Met30 ubiquitylation by Cdc53/Rbx1 in vitro is inefficient and slow, suggesting additional factors or modifications may be required for efficient ubiquitylation.
source_span: Met30 ubiquitylation in this minimal in vitro system with Cdc53/Rbx1, Cdc34, and E1 was very inefficient and required a long reaction time suggesting possible involvement of additional factors, inefficient protein folding in E. coli, or a post-translational modification lacking in this expression system.
selection_reasoning: This highlights limitations of the minimal system and points to complexity in the degradation mechanism.

fact: A Skp1-independent cullin-1 based ubiquitylation event has been suggested in human cells, indicating that the pathway described in yeast may have broader relevance.
source_span: Consistent with these results, a Skp1 independent cullin-1 based ubiquitylation event has been suggested previously in human cells where Rictor, a component of mTORC2 complex associates with Cullin-1 instead of Skp1, to form a functional E3 ubiquitin ligase that promotes ubiquitylation of SGK1.
selection_reasoning: This suggests the pathway may be evolutionarily conserved and relevant beyond yeast.

fact: The cullin Cdc53 can promote substrate ubiquitylation independently of Skp1.
source_span: The findings reported here illustrate a Skp1 independent function for the cullin Cdc53 in substrate ubiquitylation.
selection_reasoning: This is a core novel finding about the mechanism of ubiquitylation relevant to the study's main claim.

fact: A Skp1 independent cullin-1 based ubiquitylation event has been previously suggested in human cells involving Rictor and Cullin-1.
source_span: Consistent with these results, a Skp1 independent cullin-1 based ubiquitylation event has been suggested previously in human cells where Rictor, a component of mTORC2 complex associates with Cullin-1 instead of Skp1, to form a functional E3 ubiquitin ligase that promotes ubiquitylation of SGK1.
selection_reasoning: This background fact supports the biological relevance and conservation of the Skp1-independent ubiquitylation mechanism.

fact: The study sheds light on the regulation and complexity of E3 ubiquitin ligases and suggests additional diversity in the cullin-RING family of ubiquitin ligases.
source_span: Together, our findings shed light on the regulation and complexity of E3 ligases and suggest additional diversity in the cullin-RING family of ubiquitin ligases.
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the significance and broader impact of the findings.

fact: Yeast strains isogenic to 15DaubΔ were used as the model organism in this study.
source_span: Yeast strains used in this study are isogenic to 15DaubΔ, a bar1Δ ura3Δns; a derivative of BF264-15D.
selection_reasoning: This provides essential background on the biological system used to investigate the ubiquitylation mechanism.

fact: Protein degradation rates were measured using cycloheximide chase and galactose shut-off experiments.
source_span: Determination of protein degradation rates was done using cycloheximide chase experiments and galactose shut-off experiments.
selection_reasoning: This high-level method description is relevant to understanding how the study assessed protein stability related to ubiquitylation.

fact: Skp1 protein levels were depleted in yeast cells by shifting from galactose to dextrose media to study Skp1-independent interactions.
source_span: For in vitro binding assay with yeast lysates, yeast cells containing a GAL1-controlled SKP1 allele and expressing endogenous TAP-tagged Cdc53 were grown in YEP galactose overnight, washed and then transferred to YEP dextrose media for 12 hours to deplete Skp1 protein levels.
selection_reasoning: This experimental approach is key to demonstrating the Skp1-independent function of Cdc53.
